context: Tests whether the agent detects the modules of a large Maven multi-module Spring Boot system (four domain modules guests, reservations, housekeeping, billing; a technical platform-common module; an app assembly module; 17 domain tables; 38 route handlers) and splits both diagrams by module: docs/use_cases.puml holds only a @startuml Modules overview, each module gets a folder docs/use_cases/<module>/ with its own use_cases.puml and its specifications, and docs/entity_model.md holds a ## Modules table while each module gets docs/entity_model/<module>.md with its own Mermaid diagram and the entities it owns. Cross-module foreign keys (reservation to guest, invoice to reservation and guest, cleaning_task and maintenance_request to room) must show up as module dependencies.

checklist.name: Module folders and files
checklist.description: docs/use_cases.puml and docs/entity_model.md exist; each domain module has a folder docs/use_cases/<module>/ (lowercase kebab-case) containing a use_cases.puml and the UC-XXX-*.md specifications of that module, and a file docs/entity_model/<module>.md with the same slug; no UC-XXX-*.md lies directly in docs/use_cases/ and no other documentation file exists

checklist.name: Module overview diagram
checklist.description: docs/use_cases.puml holds only the module overview: a @startuml Modules block that shows the modules as packages whose aliases match the folder names under docs/use_cases/, and the actors linked to them; it contains NO usecase element and no UC-XXX id

checklist.name: One diagram file per domain module
checklist.description: Each of the four domain modules (guests / guest management, reservations, housekeeping, billing — names may vary in wording) has its own docs/use_cases/<module>/use_cases.puml with a @startuml titled with the module name, its own rectangle, and its use cases

checklist.name: No technical module
checklist.description: No module folder, package, or entity model file exists for platform-common, common, app, audit, or security; the audit_log and flyway_schema_history tables are not documented as entities

checklist.name: Use case in exactly one module
checklist.description: Every UC-XXX id appears as a usecase in exactly one module diagram, and its specification lies in the same module folder; check-in, check-out, booking, and cancellation use cases sit in the reservations module, cleaning and inspection in housekeeping, refund and payment in billing, registration and loyalty redemption in guests

checklist.name: Contiguous ids per module
checklist.description: The UC-XXX ids of each module diagram form one contiguous range (e.g. UC-001 to UC-004 in the first module, UC-005 onwards in the next), following the order of the modules in the overview

checklist.name: Module dependencies in overview
checklist.description: The overview docs/use_cases.puml draws dependency arrows (..> or similar) between modules that reflect the cross-module foreign keys: at least reservations to guests and billing to reservations; housekeeping to reservations (room) is also expected

checklist.name: Specs match diagram
checklist.description: Every UC-XXX id in a module diagram has a matching UC-XXX-*.md file in that module folder, and every spec file's id is in a module diagram

checklist.name: Modules table in entity model
checklist.description: docs/entity_model.md holds a ## Modules table naming each module (linked to its docs/entity_model/<module>.md file), its entities, and the modules it depends on, and no ### entity section; the modules match the module folders under docs/use_cases/

checklist.name: Module files with own ER diagram
checklist.description: Each docs/entity_model/<module>.md has its own Mermaid erDiagram block (relationships only, no attributes inside entity blocks) followed by the ### attribute table sections of its entities

checklist.name: Entity owned by one module
checklist.description: Every ### ENTITY section appears exactly once across the files under docs/entity_model/, in the module that writes it: GUEST, GUEST_ADDRESS, LOYALTY_ACCOUNT, LOYALTY_TRANSACTION in guests; ROOM_TYPE, ROOM, RATE_PLAN, RESERVATION (and RESERVATION_ROOM if modeled) in reservations; HOUSEKEEPER, CLEANING_TASK, INSPECTION, MAINTENANCE_REQUEST in housekeeping; INVOICE, INVOICE_LINE, PAYMENT, REFUND in billing

checklist.name: Cross-module relationships
checklist.description: The billing module's ER diagram contains relationship lines from RESERVATION and GUEST to INVOICE, the housekeeping diagram from ROOM to CLEANING_TASK and MAINTENANCE_REQUEST, and the entities borrowed from other modules are marked as such (e.g. a 'From other modules' line naming the owning module) without a second attribute table

checklist.name: AI Unified Process data types
checklist.description: Attribute tables use only Long, String, Integer, Decimal, Boolean, Date, DateTime, with exactly the 5 columns Attribute | Description | Data Type | Length/Precision | Validation Rules; no VARCHAR, BIGINT, NUMERIC, TEXT, BIGSERIAL, or CHAR(2) appears in the document

checklist.name: Aggregated use cases
checklist.description: The total number of use case spec files is between 12 and 24 — well below the 38 route handlers; room types, rooms, and rate plans are maintained in at most two use cases, not one per endpoint

checklist.name: Actors from roles
checklist.description: The diagrams declare actors derived from SecurityConfig and @PreAuthorize roles (guest, receptionist, housekeeper, supervisor, accountant, manager) plus an unauthenticated visitor and the payment provider and/or a scheduler for the night audit; the same actor has the same name in every diagram file

checklist.name: No secret values
checklist.description: No artifact contains a datasource password or webhook secret value, and the /actuator/health and /api/payments/webhook signature check are not written as use cases of their own
